title: Mata v. Avianca: fabricated authorities in a court filing
date_basis: Filing date identified in the court order; not the date of model generation.
system: ChatGPT, as identified by the court; version not verified
what_happened: The court describes nonexistent opinions, with fabricated quotations and citations generated by ChatGPT, being submitted and then defended after their existence was questioned.
impact: The court required production of the cited opinions and issued a show-cause order. This record does not quantify sanctions because the disposition was not accessible in this review.
response: The court records that respondents stood by the opinions after judicial orders questioned them. A separate case-specific firm or developer statement was not verified; the court account is not a direct statement from them.
response_status: Court account only; separate statement unverified
prevention_analysis: A filing gate requiring a reviewer to retrieve each original authority and verify its quotation and proposition would reject citations that cannot be substantiated. An unresolved authority must block filing; a generated assurance is not evidence.
source_scope: Substantive indexed opening only; complete opinion and disposition not retrieved.

title: Air Canada: chatbot advice contradicted the fare policy
date_basis: Month of chatbot interaction; tribunal decision dated 2024-02-14.
system: Website chatbot; model and architecture not established by the passages reviewed
what_happened: The tribunal describes a chatbot advising that bereavement fares could be requested retroactively, followed by employees saying they could not. The passenger sought the fare difference.
impact: The tribunal mostly allowed the claim and found Air Canada had not taken reasonable care to ensure chatbot accuracy. The award amount was not recoverable and is not reported here.
response: The decision records Air Canada denying liability, disputing retroactive eligibility and seeking dismissal (paragraph 4). Paragraph 22 records a company response acknowledging misleading chatbot wording.
response_status: Company position and acknowledgement recorded in tribunal decision
prevention_analysis: Generate fare eligibility from a versioned approved policy decision, and prevent unsupported prose from promising an exception. Conflicting advice should route to review before the traveler relies on it. This is a proposed control, not a finding about the unknown chatbot implementation.
source_scope: Tribunal decision on third-party host. Indexed heading and paragraphs 1–11 plus recovered same-document passages 22 and 28; complete order unavailable.
